blocks.title: Molar heat of vaporization
blocks.text: The amount of heat absorbed by one mole of a liquid to convert it into one mole of vapour at its boiling point at 1 atmospheric pressure is called molar heat of vapourization.
The molar heats of vaportization depends upon the strength of intermolecular forces. When one mole H₂O is converted to vapour at 100 °C, then heat absorbed is 40.6 kJ mol⁻¹.
NH₃ and HCl only need 21.7 and 15.6 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively to become vapour at their boiling points. This difference is due to the stronger intermolecular forces in water.
